sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: South-western Punjab border district, formerly known as Bangla. Known for border tourism (Sadqi Border retreat ceremony) and 1971 Indo-Pak War memory (Asafwala War Memorial) rather than palaces or temples.

places.name: Sadqi Border Retreat
places.location: ~15 km from Fazilka city, via NH-10
places.facts: Punjab's third international border retreat venue after Attari-Wagah and Hussainiwala; ceremony jointly performed by BSF and Pakistan Rangers.

places.name: Asafwala War Memorial
places.facts: Known as 'Shaheedo Ki Samadhi'; established 1972; ashes of 82 soldiers who died in the 1971 Indo-Pak War preserved here; 5-acre site with a recently added 71-foot Victory Tower.

places.name: Gol Kothi
places.location: Within a Government Senior Secondary School, Fazilka
places.facts: Built 1913 as a British recreational facility; now a heritage structure within a school campus.

places.name: Mud Fort, Abohar
places.facts: ASI-protected ancient settlement site, largely in ruins.

places.name: Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Park
places.facts: Hosts the annual Fazilka Heritage Festival.

places.name: Fazilka TV Tower
places.facts: One of the tallest structures in India; regional broadcasting tower.

places.name: Abohar Wildlife Sanctuary (Black Buck)
places.timings: Not fully detailed in Places to Visit, mentioned in banner content
places.facts: Wildlife sanctuary known for blackbuck population.

howToReach.air: Nearest major airport: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar
howToReach.road: Connected to Ferozepur, Abohar, Bathinda, Chandigarh
